Prompt to build this component

When to use it

When to use

  • To make one point with several numbers at once: shares side by side, who has what, events in order, the parts of a whole.
  • When the comparison is the point and the reader should see it before reading a value.
  • With every value written next to its mark, so the chart reads without the colours.

When not to use

  • For one number: write it large, with its label (ds-text-display and a caption), not a single bar.
  • To look up exact values across many rows and columns: use cmp-table.
  • For the state of one thing: use cmp-status-pill.
  • For progress through steps a person is taking: use cmp-step-list.
  • For numbers nobody measured. A chart shows sourced figures only; an estimate is labelled as one, with who made it.
Variants, anatomy, accessibility, interaction and content rules

Variants

  • bar — horizontal bars on one shared scale, one row per measure, each with its label and its value; rows can be grouped under a heading, such as their source. The base class alone; no modifier class.
  • matrix — rows against columns of marks: full, part or none. Use it for who has which capability, or which checks pass. The cells of a row can be grouped, for example by step.
  • timeline — dated events in order along one line, each with its date and a short label.
  • stack — one thin bar split into the parts of a whole, each part named beside its share.
  • dot — each value one dot on a shared hairline scale, one row per measure: many values compared in little space.
  • slope — before and after on one scale, one row per measure: the earlier value muted, a line to the later one, both written.
  • multiples — the same small chart repeated per item on one shared scale (small multiples), for more items than one chart holds.
  • dense — a modifier for any variant: smaller marks and no space between rows, for a long matrix or a slide's grid.

Anatomy

  • Root: <figure class="ds-chart"> (add ds-chart--matrix, --timeline, --stack, --dot, --slope or --multiples, and ds-chart--dense with any).
  • Title (optional): <figcaption class="ds-chart__title">, the point the chart makes in one line. Leave it out when a heading right above already makes the point.
  • Plot: <div class="ds-chart__plot" data-chart aria-hidden="true">, the drawn marks. The table below carries the same numbers for assistive technology. Inside the plot, sizes that are data are SVG shapes on a 0 to 100 scale (viewBox="0 0 100 4" preserveAspectRatio="none"); colours come from the classes, never from attributes.
  • bar: inside the plot, an optional <div class="ds-chart__group"> with a <span class="ds-chart__group-label">, then one <div class="ds-chart__row"> per measure, holding <span class="ds-chart__label">, <svg class="ds-chart__track" viewBox="0 0 100 4" preserveAspectRatio="none"><rect class="ds-chart__base" width="100" height="4"></rect><rect class="ds-chart__bar" width="84" height="4"></rect></svg> and <span class="ds-chart__value">. The bar's width is the value on the shared scale.
  • matrix: an optional head row <div class="ds-chart__row ds-chart__row--head"> with a <span class="ds-chart__col"> per column, then one ds-chart__row per row with its ds-chart__label and <span class="ds-chart__cells">, holding <span class="ds-chart__cell ds-chart__cell--yes|--part|--no"> marks. When there is a head row, every row's marks line up under its column names. Several ds-chart__cells in one row are groups, with a wider gap between them. The head row holds an empty ds-chart__label and one ds-chart__cells of ds-chart__col names.
  • timeline: <ol class="ds-chart__events"> in the plot, one <li class="ds-chart__event"> per event with <time class="ds-chart__date"> and <span class="ds-chart__label">.
  • stack: <svg class="ds-chart__stack" viewBox="0 0 100 4" preserveAspectRatio="none"> with one <rect class="ds-chart__seg" x="0" width="40" height="4"> per part, each starting where the last ends, then <ul class="ds-chart__legend"> with one <li> per part: <span class="ds-chart__key"></span>, its label and its ds-chart__value.
  • dot: rows as for bar, but the svg holds <line class="ds-chart__rule" x1="0" x2="100" y1="2" y2="2"> (the shared scale) and <line class="ds-chart__dot" x1="72" x2="72" y1="2" y2="2">: a zero-length line with a round cap is a dot that stays round however the plot stretches.
  • slope: each row is ds-chart__label, <span class="ds-chart__value ds-chart__value--from">, the svg (the rule, <line class="ds-chart__join" x1="40" x2="72" …>, <line class="ds-chart__dot ds-chart__dot--from" x1="40" …> and <line class="ds-chart__dot" x1="72" …>) and the later ds-chart__value.
  • multiples: <div class="ds-chart__multiples"> in the plot, one <div class="ds-chart__multiple"> per item with its ds-chart__label and its small chart: ds-chart__cells of marks, or a track.
  • Tone (optional): data-tone="success|warning|danger|info|neutral" on a bar row, a cell or a part colours its mark with the status mark colour. Without it the mark is the accent. A tone always sits beside a word: the row's label, the value or the legend.
  • Table alternative: <table class="ds-chart__table ds-visually-hidden" data-table-alt> after the plot, with a caption and the same numbers, labels and sources as the plot.
  • Source (with-source): <p class="ds-chart__source">, where the numbers come from and when they were measured ("Stack Overflow Developer Survey, 2025").

Accessibility

  • The plot is hidden from assistive technology; the table alternative holds every number with its label, so a screen reader hears the same facts as a sighted reader sees.
  • Every mark has its value or its label written beside it, so nothing is told by colour alone (fdn-color). Part and none marks differ by shape (a half fill, an outline), not only by shade.
  • Labels and values use text-default or text-muted on the surface beneath, AA in every theme; marks meet 3:1 against that surface.
  • The chart is not focusable and has no controls.

Interaction

  • Not interactive: nothing highlights on hover, so nothing suggests a click (int-04).
  • A bar or a part whose value changes eases to its new length over the settle duration; nothing plays when the chart first appears (int-04, int-06).

Content rules

  • The title, when there is one, states the point, not the topic: "Most developers use AI; few trust it", not "AI adoption".
  • Labels are short noun phrases in sentence case, at most six words. Values are written exactly as the source gives them, with their unit: "84%", "49,000", "Jul 2025".
  • Bars in one chart share one scale and one unit. Show percentages on 0 to 100; show counts against the largest.
  • Order rows the way the point reads: largest first, or the order of the source. Timeline events go oldest first.
  • Eight rows, columns or events read at the base size; up to fourteen rows take ds-chart--dense; more become small multiples. Never leave a row out to fit.
  • Name the source of every number. When the numbers come from different sources, group the rows by source.

Do and don't

  • Do give the data the ink: no gridlines, frames, shaded tracks or a legend where a word beside the mark will do.
  • Do write each value next to its mark.
  • Do keep one point per chart; a second point is a second chart.
  • Don't draw a chart for one number.
  • Don't mix units, or percentages from different bases, on one scale without grouping them under their source.
  • Don't use colour to rank; tone is for state (success, danger), and the accent is for everything else.
